styles.name: The Recorder
styles.blurb: You hold things. What was on the screen is still on the screen for you a beat after it goes, and most of what people call your attention is really just that you never quite put the last thing down.

mistake_one.title: You trust the first version
mistake_one.body: Whatever you took in first stays first, and a correction has to work twice as hard to replace it. That is why you are rarely wrong about what was said and sometimes wrong about what is true now.
mistake_one.fix: Say the new version out loud once. It files it as first.

styles.name: The Navigator
styles.blurb: You keep the map. Where a thing was gets filed with what it was, so you walk back to things other people have to go looking for, and you rarely notice you are doing it.

mistake_one.title: You navigate instead of reading
mistake_one.body: Given a list and a layout you take the layout every time, which is fast until the layout is somebody else's and they never drew you one.
mistake_one.fix: Sketch it before you start. Two minutes buys the whole task.

mistake_one.body: You know something moved a beat before you know what, and you tend to say so in that beat — which reads as certainty you have not got yet.
mistake_one.fix: Wait until you can point at it. The beat costs nothing.

sections.title: Your Brain Profile
sections.teaser_line: Which of the four rounds you actually run on, and the one you lean on when you are tired.
preview: Four scores, read off your own taps, and one place where two of them pull hard against each other.
It names the round you lead with, the one you fall back to, and which of the two you are using when you are rushing.

sections.title: What Your Weakest Round Says
sections.teaser_line: The round you dropped most, and what it is really telling you about how you take things in.
preview: It is not the round itself. It is the thing the round asks for, which shows up in about nine places a week.
The chapter names those places, and the one small change that makes most of them easier.

sections.title: 5 Sharp Strengths & 2 Blind Spots
sections.teaser_line: Five things your brain does better than most people's. And the two places it looks away.
preview: The first strength reads as obvious written down, and it still shapes more of your week than anything else on the list.
The two blind spots are ranked, and the costlier one is last.

sections.title: Your 7-Day Sharpening Plan
sections.teaser_line: One small thing a day for a week, chosen for the round you were weakest on.
preview: Seven days, each one a single thing that takes under five minutes and targets the round you actually dropped.
Every day says what it is for, so the easy ones stop reading as filler.
